c.tagline: A moonlit maze of canals and cobblestones beneath the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain.

taxi.fareNote: Didi is the way to book a car and is far easier than hailing; note the Old Town (Dayan) is pedestrian-only, so cars and taxis drop you at the gates. Metered street taxis exist but drivers sometimes prefer a flat rate.

emergency.note: 120 is the ambulance number and 119 is fire; 110 is police. English is rarely spoken, so a translation app or written Chinese address helps.

hood_landmark.Dayan Old Town: Sifang Street, Old Town of Lijiang

avoid.reason: Tout-led bar invitations and overpriced horse-trek and tea scams in the Old Town — book tours through reputable agencies.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed heart of Lijiang, an 800-year-old maze of cobbled lanes, willow-lined canals, Naxi courtyard guesthouses and the central Sifang Street, watched over by Lion Hill and the Wangu Pavilion; magical at dawn and lantern-lit at night, though busy and touristy by day.

A smaller, older and more relaxed canal town about four kilometres northwest of Dayan, once a stop on the Ancient Tea-Horse Road, now full of arty cafes, boutiques and quieter courtyard inns; a laid-back alternative to the main Old Town.

A tranquil Naxi farming village about fifteen kilometres north below the snow mountain, famous for the 600-year-old Baisha Murals and its embroidery institute, with dirt lanes, old temples and mountain views; a slow, authentic base.

Modern Lijiang beside the Old Town, with the Black Dragon Pool park and its classic snow-mountain reflection, the bus and train links, chain hotels, supermarkets and everyday services; the practical, convenient base for transport.

The scenic foothills and resort strip north of the city toward the glaciers of the 5,596-metre Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, with Ganhaizi meadow, Blue Moon Valley and the Impression Lijiang show; a nature-focused base for the mountain.

Jinjiang Inn Lijiang Qixing Street Branch

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only, as throughout China.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:30 AM to 9:00 PM; after that, use Didi or a taxi, especially for the Old Town gates and the new-town train station.
transit.note: Lijiang has no metro; getting around means city buses, Didi and taxis, plus lots of walking, as the Old Town (Dayan) is entirely pedestrian and closed to cars. Buses and Didi link the Old Town, new town, Shuhe and the snow-mountain scenic gate.
transit.pay: Pay city buses in exact-change cash or, more commonly, by scanning with Alipay or WeChat Pay; foreign visitors should set up mobile pay in advance, as cash and cards are increasingly awkward.

bus: Intercity coaches to Kunming, Dali, Shangri-La and Tiger Leaping Gorge
train: Dali-Lijiang railway and high-speed trains to Kunming

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to downtown Lijiang (~50 min)
Taxi or Didi to the Old Town (~40-50 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in mainland China and is generally not expected in restaurants, taxis or hotels.

food.name: Naxi Grilled Fish
food.desc: Whole river fish split, packed with chili, garlic and mint, then grilled or baked over coals in foil - the Naxi dish every Old Town kitchen advertises.

places.name: Heshu Restaurant
places.note: Old Town favourite for caravan-style grilled fish and stone-pot fish cooked to a house recipe.

places.name: Huama Food Street
places.note: Night-time grill street where fish and skewers are cooked in front of you.

places.name: Zhongyi Market Eateries
places.note: Local market kitchens grill fish at half the price of the tourist lanes.

food.name: Lijiang Baba
food.desc: Thick wheat flatbread fried in oil until golden and layered - savory with ham and spring onion or sweet with rose and brown sugar.

places.name: Zhongyi Market
places.note: Market griddles fry baba fresh each morning; the version locals actually buy.

places.name: Sifang Street Stalls
places.note: Central square stalls sell sweet and savory baba to eat while walking.

places.name: Huama Food Street
places.note: Evening stalls pair baba with grilled snacks and yak yoghurt.

food.name: Lijiang Chicken Hotpot
food.desc: Free-range mountain chicken stewed in a broth pot at the table with local mushrooms, potatoes and greens added as you eat.

places.name: Mu Wan
places.note: Known for a rich black-chicken and mushroom hotpot base; comfortable courtyard setting.

places.name: Naxi Courtyard Restaurants, Wuyi Street
places.note: Quieter Naxi courtyards away from the crowds doing chicken and mushroom pots.

places.name: Zhongyi Market Eateries
places.note: Plain local hotpot houses beside the market, priced for residents.

food.name: Yak Hotpot and Yak Jerky
food.desc: Highland yak simmered in a spiced copper pot, or air-dried and shredded into chewy jerky sold by the bag - a taste of the Tibetan borderlands.

places.name: Huama Food Street
places.note: Yak skewers, yak jerky and hotpot houses lined up along the night food street.

places.name: Sifang Street Stalls
places.note: Jerky vendors let you taste before buying; ask for the less-sweet spicy cut.

places.name: Shuhe Old Town Restaurants
places.note: Calmer old town with copper-pot yak hotpot in stone courtyards.

food.name: Jidou Liangfen (Chickpea Jelly)
food.desc: Lijiang's own chickpea-flour jelly, served cold in strips with chili, vinegar and pickles in summer, or pan-fried in golden slabs when it turns cold.

places.name: Zhongyi Market
places.note: Market stalls cut it fresh from the tray; the local benchmark for liangfen.

places.name: Sifang Street Stalls
places.note: Central and easy to find; ask for the fried version on cool days.

places.name: Shuhe Old Town Snack Stalls
places.note: Village stalls serve chickpea jelly alongside baba and grilled cheese.

food.name: Wild Mushroom Hotpot
food.desc: Yunnan's summer treasure - matsutake, boletus and chanterelle simmered in chicken stock, cooked to strict timings by the server.

places.name: Mu Wan
places.note: Mushroom hotpot specialist with a black-chicken broth base; strong local following.

places.name: Zhongyi Market
places.note: See the day's fungi haul at the stalls, then eat at the kitchens around it.

places.name: Shuhe Old Town Restaurants
places.note: Courtyard restaurants doing wild mushroom pots in peak season, July to October.

food.name: Yinjiu (Naxi Rice Wine)
food.desc: Lijiang's amber fermented rice wine, low in alcohol, faintly sweet and traditionally warmed - poured at Naxi celebrations and courtyard dinners.

places.name: Naxi Courtyard Restaurants, Wuyi Street
places.note: Family courtyards serve house yinjiu by the jug with Naxi set menus.

places.name: Sifang Street Wine Shops
places.note: Shops let you taste yinjiu and plum wines before buying a bottle.

places.name: Shuhe Old Town Restaurants
places.note: Quieter old town where yinjiu comes warmed with hotpot in the evenings.

food.name: Butter Tea and Yak Yoghurt Drinks
food.desc: Tibetan-style salted butter tea from the nearby highlands, plus tart yak-milk yoghurt drinks sold cold across the Old Town.

places.name: Huama Food Street
places.note: Yak yoghurt bars and Tibetan tea stalls open into the night.

places.name: Zhongyi Market
places.note: Dairy vendors sell fresh yak yoghurt by the cup at market prices.

places.name: Shuhe Old Town Teahouses
places.note: Small teahouses pour butter tea and pu-erh in restored courtyards.

landmarks: Lijiang Old Town (Dayan Ancient Town)
A UNESCO-listed maze of cobbled lanes, gurgling canals, and tile-roofed Naxi houses, this 800-year-old trading town is one of China's most atmospheric historic quarters.
Black Dragon Pool Park (Heilongtan)
This serene park frames China's most famous mountain reflection: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain mirrored in a spring-fed pool behind the arched Suocui Bridge and Deyue Pavilion.
Mu Family Mansion (Mufu Palace)
The lavishly rebuilt palace of Lijiang's hereditary Naxi rulers climbs Lion Hill in a procession of halls and gardens dubbed the 'Forbidden City of the South.'
Wangu Tower on Lion Hill
Crowning the hill above the old town, this five-story wooden pagoda rewards the climb with sweeping views over a sea of grey-tiled rooftops to snow peaks.
Shuhe Ancient Town
Quieter than Dayan, this UNESCO-protected Tea Horse Road village keeps its stone bridges, willow-lined streams, and Naxi courtyards at a mellower, more local pace.
Baisha Village and Murals
The Naxi kingdom's original capital preserves 600-year-old temple frescoes blending Buddhist, Taoist, and Dongba imagery beneath uninterrupted views of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain.
Blue Moon Valley (Lanyue Gu)
At the foot of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, glacial meltwater pools in impossibly turquoise terraces that cascade over white limestone shoals like a miniature Jiuzhaigou.
Sifang Street (Square Market)
The old town's pulsing central plaza, once the Tea Horse Road's trading hub, fills nightly with Naxi circle dances, lanterns, and snack vendors.
Big Water Wheel
Twin wooden waterwheels turning at the entrance to Lijiang Old Town, one of the most photographed spots in the city and a popular meeting point.
Naxi Ancient Music Association
A theatre in the old town where musicians perform Baisha xiyue, an ancient courtly music tradition preserved by Lijiang's Naxi community for centuries.

train.note: Lijiang has no international trains. From Lijiang Railway Station in the new town, high-speed trains reach Dali in about 2 hours and Kunming in around 3-3.5 hours, while the Lijiang-Shangri-La railway (opened November 2023) runs north toward Shangri-La in about 1.25 hours; slower overnight sleeper trains also serve Kunming. Book on 12306 with your passport, and note the station is several kilometres south of the Old Town so allow time for the shuttle bus or taxi.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Lijiang. Long-distance buses from the Lijiang bus stations run to Kunming (about 8 hours), Dali (about 3 hours), the Tiger Leaping Gorge trailheads and Shangri-La, a common way to reach the mountain scenery north and west of the city. Tickets are sold at the terminal counters on production of a passport, and the Tiger Leaping Gorge minibuses fill early in the morning.

ferry.note: Lijiang is an inland town in the mountains of northwest Yunnan; the Jinsha (upper Yangtze) river nearby runs through the Tiger Leaping Gorge and is far too violent to navigate, so there are no passenger ferries.

half.name: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
half.blurb: The glacier-capped 5,596-metre massif north of the city, reached by cable cars to Glacier Park, with Blue Moon Valley, Ganhaizi meadow and the open-air Impression Lijiang show.

half.name: Lashihai Wetland
half.blurb: A highland lake and bird reserve about eight kilometres from town, known for horse riding along the old Tea-Horse Road and boating among migratory waterfowl.

half.name: Yuhu Village & Joseph Rock's Residence
half.blurb: A stone Naxi village at the foot of the snow mountain, home to the former house of botanist-explorer Joseph Rock, who chronicled Naxi culture for National Geographic.

full.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge
full.blurb: One of the world's deepest river canyons, where the Jinsha (upper Yangtze) roars between towering peaks; a spectacular high-trail trek about two hours north.

full.name: Shangri-La (Zhongdian)
full.blurb: A Tibetan-plateau town of monasteries, grasslands and the Ganden Sumtseling Gompa, gateway to the eastern Himalaya, a few hours north by bus or the new railway.

full.name: Lugu Lake
full.blurb: A serene alpine lake on the Sichuan border, home to the matrilineal Mosuo people and their 'walking marriage' traditions, a long but memorable day or overnight trip.
